facts.statement: Chubutisaurus possessed a more robust radius bone compared to the dinosaur Venenosaurus.
facts.quote: Chubutisaurus had a more robust radius than Venenosaurus.

facts.statement: Fossils of Chubutisaurus were first discovered in 1961 by a local farmer named Mr. Martinez near El Escorial village in Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Fossils of Chubutisaurus were first discovered in 1961 by Mr. Martinez, a local farmer near El Escorial village in Chubut Province, Patagonia in central Argentina.

facts.statement: Guillermo del Corro scientifically described the remains and named the new species Chubutisaurus insignis in 1975.
facts.quote: In 1975, del Corro scientifically described the remains and assigned them to a new genus and species of sauropod, which he named Chubutisaurus insignis.

facts.statement: The name Chubutisaurus combines the province of Chubut where it was found with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name Chubutisaurus derives from Chubut, the province the fossils were found in, and the Latin root "sauros" meaning "lizard", a common suffix for dinosaur names.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Chubutisaurus consists of a single incomplete and disarticulated individual found across multiple expeditions.
facts.quote: The holotype (name-bearing) specimen of Chubutisaurus comes from a single incomplete and disarticulated individual which was unearthed over several expeditions.

facts.statement: In 1993, paleontologist Leonardo Salgado redescribed Chubutisaurus and reinterpreted it as an indeterminate sauropod.
facts.quote: In 1993, paleontologist Leonardo Salgado redescribed Chubutisaurus and reinterpreted it as an indeterminate sauropod.

facts.statement: In 2011, Jose Carballido and colleagues described new fossils in detail and concluded they belonged to the same holotype individual.
facts.quote: In 2011, these fossils, along with previously undescribed elements, were described in detail by paleontologist Jose Carballido and colleagues who concluded that they all belonged to the holotype individual.

facts.statement: Fossils from the 1991 and 2007 expeditions were cataloged at the Museo Paleontológico 'Egidio Feruglio', meaning the holotype is now split among three institutions.
facts.quote: The fossils unearthed by the 1991 and 2007 trips were cataloged at the Museo Paleontológico 'Egidio Feruglio' under MPEF-PV 1129, meaning that the holotype of Chubutisaurus is deposited in three institutions.

facts.statement: Chubutisaurus was a somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) period found in the Cerro Barcino Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Chubutisaurus (meaning "Chubut lizard") is a genus of somphospondylan sauropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) Cerro Barcino Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: Chubutisaurus lived during the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Chubutisaurus is known from the Cerro Barcino Formation, which dates to the Cenomanian age of the late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Chubutisaurus was initially placed in the Brachiosauridae but is now considered a primitive titanosaur related to Late Cretaceous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Este gran saurópodo de aproximadamente 23 metros de largo fue colocado dentro de los braquiosáuridos, aunque actualmente se lo considera que es un titanosaurio primitivo, por lo tanto más emparentados con los dinosaurios que abundaron a finales del Cretácico.

facts.statement: While initially dated to 112-93 million years ago, later dating places Chubutisaurus solely in the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Inicialmente sus restos habían sido datados con una antigüedad de entre 112 y 93 millones de años atrás, entre el Cretácico inferior e inicios del superior, aunque posteriores dataciones del lugar parecen colocarlo solo durante finales del Cretácico.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Chubutisaurus to be 18 meters long and weigh 12 tons in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul gave a length of 18 m and a weight of 12 t.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated the length of Chubutisaurus at 23 meters in 2012.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz estimated its length at 23 m in 2012.

facts.statement: Chubutisaurus is classified within the unranked family Somphospondyli.
The species name insignis means "remarkable" in Latin.
facts.quote: Fue llamado Chubutisaurus por haber sido encontrado su esqueleto fósil en Chubut, una de las provincias que conforman la patagonia argentina.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the time range of Chubutisaurus as Aptian to Albian (119.57 to 110.1 million years ago), which contradicts other sources placing it in the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (119.57 to 110.1 million years ago)
